subject: Cloud Computing
title: Spot Instances and Preemptible VMs
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Spot Instances and Preemptible VMs.

hook.text: AWS has spare servers sitting idle. They sell them at 90% off — but they can take them back any time.

buildup.text: Spot instances are leftover cloud capacity sold at steep discounts. The catch: they can vanish with two minutes' notice.

discovery.text: Google calls them preemptible VMs. Azure calls them spot VMs. All work the same: cheap but unreliable.

twist.text: Companies that design for interruption — batch jobs, rendering, data analysis — save fortunes on spot.

climax.text: Spot pricing fluctuates like a stock market. Savvy teams bid strategically and tolerate interruptions.

punchline.text: Spot is 90% cheaper. If your workload survives interruptions.

quiz.question: What is the main risk of using spot instances?
options: The cloud provider can reclaim them with very little notice
They run at half the speed of regular instances
Data stored on spot instances is never encrypted

details.summary: Spot instances use spare cloud capacity at discounts of up to 90 percent but can be reclaimed by the provider with short notice. They are ideal for fault-tolerant workloads like batch processing, CI/CD, and distributed computing that can handle interruptions.
details.whyItMatters: Spot instances offer the deepest discounts in cloud computing. Architectures designed to handle interruptions can save enormous amounts on compute-heavy workloads.
takeaways: Discounts of up to 90 percent on compute costs
Instances can be reclaimed with two minutes' notice

faq.question: What workloads are best suited for spot instances?
faq.answer: Batch processing, CI/CD pipelines, data processing, machine learning training with checkpointing, rendering, and any workload that can save progress and resume after interruption. Stateless web servers behind load balancers can also use spot with proper draining.

faq.question: How do you handle spot instance interruptions?
faq.answer: Use interruption notices to gracefully drain connections or checkpoint work. Spread workloads across multiple instance types and availability zones to reduce simultaneous interruption risk. Combine spot with on-demand instances for a reliable baseline.
